# IYAKKI feature matrix

The single place to see what exists, what is half-done, what is next and what is on its way out.
It is written for people **and** for code assistants: one row per feature, a stable ID, the phase it belongs to,
how far along it is, and the unit tests that prove it. `crates/iyakki-core/tests/feature_matrix.rs` checks this file,
so a row cannot claim a test that does not exist or a status that contradicts its progress.

**Totals:** <!-- summary:start -->done 380 · partial 878 · planned 50 · blocked 0 · deprecated 28 · total 1336<!-- summary:end -->

## How to use it

| You want to… | Do this |
|---|---|
| **Prioritise** | Take `planned` and `partial` rows, sort by `Pri` (P0 first), then by `Progress` (finish the nearly-done first). `blocked` rows say why in Notes. |
| **Start a feature** | Set Status `partial`, Progress above 0, and add the tests you write to the `Tests` column in the same change. |
| **Finish a feature** | Status `done`, Progress `100%`, and at least one test (or a `script:` check for things only a VM can prove). |
| **Deprecate** | Set Status `deprecated` and write what replaces it in Notes (`Replaced by F-…`). Leave the row in place until the code is removed; then delete the row in the same change. |
| **Add a feature** | New row with the next free number in its area. IDs never change and are never reused. |
| **Check your edit** | `cargo test -p iyakki-core --test feature_matrix` (also runs in `cargo test --workspace`). |

**Columns.** *ID* `F-<AREA>-<nn>`. *Phase*: P0 cross-cutting · P1 core + WASM · P2 snapshots and memory · P3 hardware and editor model · P4 packaging, network, swarm · P5 shell and permissions · P6 AI services (models, RAG, vault, MCP) · P7 assistant (chat sessions, skills, agent, voice) · P8 code editor · P9 persistence · P10 web and cloud. *Status*: `done` · `partial` · `planned` · `blocked` · `deprecated`. *Pri*: P0 critical … P3 nice to have. *Tests*: `crate::path::test_name` (the crate directory is `crates/<crate>`); `script:` entries are files that perform a check outside `cargo test` (QEMU boots, audits) and must exist.

| Unit-tested with fake clocks, fake engines that report a WAV length and a fake voice that reports words; **no sound was heard** (no audio device here). Exact only where the browser voice fires `boundary` events; for every other engine the word is an estimate (see `docs/VOICE.md` for how to judge it by ear and where to tune `UNIT_MS` and the pauses). Drift fix (2026-10-27): the estimate is built in one place for TALES and the chat (both read through `story::Reader`): `WordTimeline::fitted_pinned` measures the pauses in the sound (silences of 60 ms or more in the loudness list) and pins them to the commas, dashes and full stops of the text, so the words between two pins are spread over exactly the speech between them (a wrong word weight can no longer grow through the whole sentence); abbreviations (Dr., Mr.) get no sentence pause and numbers a spoken length; the clock never leaps more than 4 words in one correction. The sentence log line now ends with the word timeline stretch factor and the worst estimated-versus-pinned boundary error; a per-word line is written at DEBUG only. Tested against synthetic voices (max 120 ms off); a real voice on the Mac is not yet heard. Device finding (2026-10-27): the engine's 32-bit float WAV (Kokoro through Lemonade) was not read by `voice::parse_wav`, so a sentence had no length, no loudness and no fit at all (log: "sound 0 ms", timeline "-"); it is now read (float, 24/32-bit and 8-bit are brought to 16-bit), which also lets the Whisper alignment run. The sentence log names the timeline that ran (engine/aligned word times, pinned N pauses, plain fit: no loudness / no silences, rate estimate). While a word is read aloud the display loop polls every 6 ms and paints the new word as a tile-only frame at once (not at the next 33 ms heartbeat); an idle TALES screen redraws every 250 ms instead of every 100 ms; the frame statistics line gives the slowest tile-only frame. Not yet seen on the Mac: the ~74 ms "clock behind the sound" figure is jitter of the mixer's heard position, which the in-process mixer test does not reproduce. |

NOT proven on hardware: that the image's alsa-lib has the `file` plugin, that GStreamer's `alsasink` keeps a steady audio clock on a null-backed PCM (sound and video may drift), the latency, and that the engine's user may open the pipe. Off by default; if the browser goes silent, turn it off. Replaces the gap of F-SND-12 for the web engine only (the media player is not covered). Root cause of the Mac mini silence proven 2026-11-06: the engine's `web-alsa-mix.conf` includes `alsa.conf`, whose hooks load `/etc/asound.conf` AFTER ours, so the system `pcm.!default` (softvol over the exclusive `plughw:0,0`) won and the engine got EBUSY while the radio held the card. Fix: `IYAKKI_WEBSINK_DEVICE=iyakkiwebmix` makes the sink open our PCM by name, and the status line names the route. Hardware retest pending (radio and TikTok together; lip-sync and latency still unproven). |
